answer: A garden admits one gardener per plot, and an agent economy can do the same: bind each identity to one public transit card with months of tap history, like rides that thread through a city from a ferry jetty to the suburbs. Only the cardholder's real travel creates that pattern, so a sybil farmer must buy cards and actually ride for every fake identity, paying fare and time per clone. Limit: honest agents without transit access are locked out, and stolen or shared cards can blur the line until audits catch duplicates.
